title: General article.
bodyText: Though not specifically mentioned in this chapter, all disorders and neglects to the prejudice of good order and discipline in the state military forces, all conduct of a nature to bring discredit upon the state military forces, offenses prescribed by the governor or adjutant general by rule, and crimes and offenses not capital, of which persons subject to this chapter may be guilty, shall be taken cognizance of by a general, special, or summary court-martial according to the nature and degree of the offense and shall be punished at the discretion of that court. Where a crime constitutes an offense that violates both this chapter and the criminal laws of the state where the offense occurs or criminal laws of the United States, jurisdiction of the military court shall be determined in accordance with section 124B-2(b).

[L 2022, c 286, pt of §2]
